paths.description: Next up, we need to determine where to find your content, and where to store the Stash database, generated files and cache files. These settings can be changed later if needed.
paths.path_to_blobs_directory_empty_for_defaul: path to blobs directory (empty for default)
paths.path_to_cache_directory_empty_for_defaul: path to cache directory (empty for default)
paths.path_to_generated_directory_empty_for_de: path to generated directory (empty for default)
paths.sfw_content_settings_description: stash can be used to manage SFW content such as photography, art, comics, and more. Enabling this option will adjust some UI behaviour to be more appropriate for SFW content.
paths.stash_alert: No library paths have been selected. No media will be able to be scanned into Stash. Are you sure?
paths.where_can_stash_store_blobs: Where can Stash store database binary data?
paths.where_can_stash_store_blobs_description: Stash can store binary data such as scene covers, performer, studio and tag images either in the database or in the filesystem. By default, it will store this data in the filesystem in the subdirectory blobs within the directory containing your config file. If you want to change this, please enter an absolute or relative (to the current working directory) path. Stash will create this directory if it does not already exist.
paths.where_can_stash_store_blobs_description_: Alternatively, you can store this data in the database. Note: This will increase the size of your database file, and will increase database migration times.
paths.where_can_stash_store_cache_files: Where can Stash store cache files?
paths.where_can_stash_store_cache_files_descri: In order for some functionality like HLS/DASH live transcoding to function, Stash requires a cache directory for temporary files. By default, Stash will create a cache directory within the directory containing your config file. If you want to change this, please enter an absolute or relative (to the current working directory) path. Stash will create this directory if it does not already exist.
paths.where_can_stash_store_its_database: Where can Stash store its database?
paths.where_can_stash_store_its_database_descr: Stash uses an SQLite database to store your content metadata. By default, this will be created as stash-go.sqlite in the directory containing your config file. If you want to change this, please enter an absolute or relative (to the current working directory) filename.
paths.where_can_stash_store_its_database_warni: WARNING: storing the database on a different system to where Stash is run from (e.g. storing the database on a NAS while running the Stash server on another computer) is unsupported! SQLite is not intended for use across a network, and attempting to do so can very easily cause your entire database to become corrupted.
paths.where_can_stash_store_its_generated_cont: Where can Stash store its generated content?

In order to provide thumbnails, previews and sprites, Stash generates images and videos. This also includes transcodes for unsupported file formats. By default, Stash will create a generated directory within the directory containing your config file. If you want to change where this generated media will be stored, please enter an absolute or relative (to the current working directory) path. Stash will create this directory if it does not already exist.
paths.where_is_your_porn_located_description: Add directories containing your videos and images. Stash will use these directories to find videos and images during scanning.

success.help_links: If you run into issues or have any questions or suggestions, feel free to open an issue in the {githubLink}, or ask the community in the {discordLink}.

Alternatively, you can supply paths to the ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries in the System Settings. These binaries must be present for Stash to function.
success.next_config_step_one: You will be taken to the Configuration page next. This page will allow you to customize what files to include and exclude, set a username and password to protect your system, and a whole bunch of other options.

success.open_collective: Check out our {open_collective_link} to see how you can contribute to the continued development of Stash.
success.welcome_contrib: We also welcome contributions in the form of code (bug fixes, improvements and new features), testing, bug reports, improvement and feature requests, and user support. Details can be found in the Contribution section of the in-app manual.
success.your_system_has_been_created: Success! Your system has been created!
